title: Video by thedragonfish.dark
description:
This image features a tweet from journalist Clive Thompson highlighting a mischievous alternative to standard link shorteners called "Shady URL." The post explains that instead of making a link clean and concise, this tool transforms any normal URL into something that looks intentionally suspicious—or, as Clive puts it, a site "crawling with syphilitic javascript." An included screenshot shows a real-world example: a harmless personal website is converted into a string of text that looks like a credit score scam or an auto-initiated download. The service’s tagline, "Don’t just shorten your URL, make it suspicious and frightening," perfectly captures the chaotic energy of early-internet prank culture.
​#InternetCulture #CyberSecurityHumor #PrankTools #WebDevelopment #ShadyURL
